newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty just down vs basket, money mkt squeeze eases.
newsitem.headline: Zloty just down vs basket, money mkt squeeze eases.

text.p: The Polish zloty held flat in early trade after opening stronger against the basket of currencies 2.80/2.76 percent from the trading band centre, dealers said.
They said the zloty should continue to trade in a tight range around 2.7 percent from the parity rate, underpinned by tight money market and stable dollar/mark rate.

"The zloty should fluctuate around last few days' level of 2.7 percent from the parity and rangebound dollar/mark should keep the zloty stable later in the day," said Jerzy Wyjadowski from Bank Slaski SA.

At 1015 GMT the zloty was quoted at 2.80/2.76 percent from the trading band centre against opening's 2.86/2.75 percent. It was at 2.8635/45 to the dollar, down from opening's 2.8610/40 and at 1.8399/06 to the mark against 1.8390/15.

One-day deposit rates eased three points at bid and dealers said cash inflows from retailers might have eased the two-week money market squeeze but said it was still too early to say whether the drop in rates signalled the end of the drought.
At 0945 GMT overnight rates were at 22.50/24.50 percent, down from opening's 24.80/24.90 percent, tomorrow/next traded at 22.00/24.50 percent, down from 24.80/24.95 percent.

"After the first wave of cash outflows at the beginning of December due increased end-of-year spendings money is now starting to flow back from the retail sector and now we may have a mixture of the two," said one dealer at a Polish bank.

Dealers added that some banks may have started to let out reserve funds after they failed to purchase T-bills on Monday's primary tender, as the finance ministry rejected more than 300 million zlotys worth of bids.
They said low volume of deals and big spreads on money market signalled market's uncertainty about equilibrium levels.
